summary: Jules Brooks Levinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia in 1994, supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins, and was an assistant professor of religion at Hamline University (attested 1996).

Jules Luquiens (1845–1899) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Geneva and Yale University (Ph.D. 1873) under William Dwight Whitney, later serving as professor at MIT (1875–1892) and Yale (1892–1899).

Jules Marouzeau (1878–1964) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet at the Sorbonne. He served as directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1920) and professor of Latin at the Sorbonne (1925–1948).

Jules Michelet (1798–1874) was a French historian educated at Lycée Charlemagne. He held posts at the École Normale Supérieure (1827), the Archives nationales (1830–1851), and served as professor of history at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

Jules Oppert (1825–1905) worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Bonn under Lassen and Freytag, and Kiel (Ph.D. 1847), he served as professor at INALCO (1857) and the Collège de France (1874–1905).

Jules Pierre Barthoux (1881–1965) was a scholar in archaeology and Iranian/Central Asian studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Lille in 1922. He headed the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan from 1923 to 1933.
Jules Thonnelier (d. 1879) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held memberships in the Société Asiatique and the Société de l'histoire de France.

Julia A. B. Hegewald (born 1971) is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned her BA and PhD from SOAS University of London, an MA from Oxford, and completed her habilitation at RWTH Aachen University in 2008.

Julia Ching (1934–2001) was a scholar of sinology, religion, and philosophy. Educated at Catholic University of America and the Australian National University (Ph.D.), she taught at Columbia and Yale before becoming a professor at the University of Toronto in 1978.
Julia F. Andrews (born 1951) is a specialist in sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Brown, Harvard, and UC Berkeley, and joined the faculty at Ohio State University around 1987.

Julia König is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Jena from 2006 to 2013 and held a post there in the Faculty of Social and Behavioral Sciences from 2008 to 2009.

Julia Leslie (1948–2004) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Sussex and Oxford. She held posts at Harvard and Oxford, and served as lecturer and reader at SOAS University of London from 1990 to 2004.
Julian Schott is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. By 2026, he is attested as a faculty member at the University of Vienna and a research fellow at the University of Hamburg.

Juliane Schober is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989. She held associate professor posts in religious studies at Arizona State University (attested 1997, 2007).
Julie Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds and held a post at Miami University (attested 2011).

Julien Girard de Rialle (1841–1904) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes and under Honoré-Joseph Chavée, later lecturing at the Sorbonne.

Julien Levesque is an Indology and history scholar who earned a PhD from EHESS (2016). He held posts at CSH (2017–2021), Ashoka University (2021–2022), the University of Zurich (2022–2025), and CNRS (2025).

Julien Vinson (1843–1926) was an Indologist and linguist educated at the École Nationale du Génie Rural, des Eaux et des Forêts. From 1879 to 1921, he served as professor of Hindustani and Tamil at INALCO.

Julieta Rotaru is an Indologist and linguist who earned her PhD at the University of Bucharest. She held posts at the University of Bucharest, the Bucharest Metropolitan Library, Södertörn University, and INALCO in 2021.

Julius Dutoit (1872–1958) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich, Giessen, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (Ph.D. 1898) under Adalbert and Ernst Kuhn. He served as director of Riemenschneider-Gymnasium from 1929 to 1934.
